city.name: Kyoto
city.description: Central Kyoto from open data: Kyoto Station to the Imperial Palace, lit by the real sun, with measured building heights from Project PLATEAU.

tour.title: Kyoto from open data
tour.text: {buildings} buildings from OpenStreetMap, Overture Maps and Project PLATEAU, on GSI 5 m laser terrain under GSI aerial photographs. The grid is Heian-kyo's: streets laid out in the year 794.

tour.title: Kyoto Tower
tour.text: 131 m to the spire, with the observation deck at 100 m: a steel tube with no frame inside it, finished in 1964. The model draws it from those figures; PLATEAU gives its footprint block as {landmark:kyoto_tower.plateau_m} m because it records the tower and the hotel below it as one building.

tour.title: Higashi Honganji
tour.text: The Founder's Hall, the Goei-do, is one of the largest wooden buildings in the world. It stands among low roofs: most of this city is under 10 m.

tour.title: A city that stays low
tour.text: {buildings} buildings, the median measured at 8.4 m. Only 1,305 reach above 31 m and 63 above 45 m. Kyoto's skyline rules hold the centre down, so Kyoto Tower and the station stand out.

tour.title: A winter day on the roofs
tour.text: 21 December, 8 am to 4 pm. The sun never climbs above 31.6° here, so even a 20 m block throws a shadow of 33 m at noon.

tour.title: Imperial Gardens in winter
tour.text: On 21 December at noon, {sun:京都御苑|12-21|12:00}% of the Kyoto Gyoen gets direct sun; on 21 June, {sun:京都御苑|6-21|12:00}%.

tour.title: Kamo River at dusk
tour.text: Autumn, 4:20 pm. The sun sets behind the western hills and the river valley fills with shadow before the streets do.

protection.title: No statutory sun rule for public places
protection.summary: Kyoto protects its skyline with height limits (a cap of 31 m in the busiest districts) and Japan limits shadows on homes with the Building Standards Act, but neither protects sun on parks. Sun on these places is measured for information, not tested against a rule.
protection.source_note: No legal window is transcribed for these places, so each is shown for 10:00-14:00 and none is marked protected.
protection.reading_note: Heights come from Project PLATEAU, measured from aerial survey in 2020-2021, so buildings finished since are missing or low.
protection.tip: Tip: try a plot just south of the Imperial Gardens in winter.
